panels.description: Share of incidents answered INSTANTLY from the knowledge base (recall) vs a full investigation. The headline learning-loop KPI — it should climb as the catalog compounds.
panels.title: Recall fire-rate

panels.description: Of the recalls that fired, the share the adversarial verify pass kept at full confidence (vs downgraded/rejected). A low value means recalls fire but don't hold up — check confirm evidence / entry quality.
panels.title: Recall precision

panels.description: Recalls that were followed by the incident actually resolving. This is the ground-truth trust signal that drives outcome decay.
panels.title: Recall resolve-rate

panels.description: Share of an investigation's model tokens that a delivered recall short-circuit avoids: 1 - (tokens per recall / tokens per full-loop investigation), both provider-reported over the dashboard range. MEASURED on both sides — not an assumed budget ceiling. Negative means a recall currently costs more than the loop it replaced (check the reranker and verify token counts). The "Token cost: full loop vs recall" panel shows the two raw means.
panels.title: Recall token savings

panels.description: Structurally-invalid entries at the MOST RECENT catalog index (6m window ≈ one git-sync). >0 means entries are silently dropped from recall — fix them (see `lore validate-kb`).
panels.title: Invalid KB entries

panels.description: Every fired recall by the verify pass's verdict: verified (kept), downgraded (confidence lowered), rejected (withdrawn → fell through to a full investigation). Watch the downgraded share.
panels.title: Recall outcome by verify result

panels.description: Why a candidate did NOT short-circuit: low_outcome (trust decayed), rerank_low_confidence / rerank_no_signal (reranker), low_margin (BM25). The diagnostic for 'recall never fires'.
panels.title: Recall rejections by reason

panels.description: Answer source over time: recall (instant) vs fresh (full investigation).
panels.title: Recall vs fresh (answer mix)

panels.description: Distribution of BM25 recall scores at the decision point. Use this to tune min_score.
panels.title: Recall score distribution (BM25)

panels.description: Investigations recorded in the outcome ledger (by kind) and incidents later resolved.
panels.title: Outcomes opened & incidents resolved

panels.description: Open to resolve duration percentiles.
panels.title: Incident resolution time (p50 / p95)

panels.description: Outcome of resolved incidents whose original answer was a recall short-circuit.
panels.title: Recall outcome by result

panels.description: Curation pass outcomes (catalog writes / dedup skips) by kind and result.
panels.title: Curation rate by kind & result

panels.description: Catalog top-hit BM25 score at the curation dedup decision. Use this to tune the dedup threshold: high scores mean a near-duplicate entry already exists.
panels.title: Curation dedup score distribution (BM25)

panels.description: Mean provider-reported tokens (input incl. cached + output) per investigation, split by whether a recall short-circuited it. The GAP between the two lines IS the saving — both are measured the same way, over the same window, per investigation. The full-loop line filters {result!="recall"} so it excludes the very runs it is being compared against; without that filter it would contain them and the apparent saving would shrink as recall improved. A window with no investigations of a given kind reads as no-data, not zero.
panels.title: Token cost: full loop vs recall

panels.description: Estimated USD per investigation (only populated when model.pricing is set). Recalls cost a fraction of a full loop.
panels.title: Per-investigation cost (USD)

panels.description: Share of input tokens served from the provider prompt cache — higher is cheaper/faster.
panels.title: Model cache hit ratio

panels.description: nudge = the run was forced to conclude early but still delivered findings; kill = hard-stopped (result=budget_exceeded). A nudged investigation completes and records result=resolved like any other, so it is invisible in every other series — this is the only panel that shows a ceiling silently truncating investigations. Alert on the nudge series.
panels.title: Spend-ceiling trips by stage

panels.description: tokens_request = the next single request alone exceeded a quarter of max_tokens_per_investigation; tokens_total = the run's cumulative tokens did; cost = max_cost_per_investigation (needs model.pricing). One run reports one reason — the ceiling that first engaged the ladder is latched from nudge through kill — so this names the knob to raise.
panels.title: Which ceiling is binding (by reason)

panels.description: Investigations started, requeued by the rate limiter, and dropped (max requeues / budget kill).
panels.title: Investigation start/throttle/drop rate

panels.description: Investigation wall-clock duration percentiles.
panels.title: Investigation duration (p50 / p95 / p99)

panels.description: Completed investigations by result.
panels.title: Investigation completion rate by result

panels.description: Tool invocation rate by tool.
panels.title: Tool call rate by tool

panels.description: Fraction of tool calls returning result=error.
panels.title: Tool error ratio

panels.description: p95 tool call latency by tool.
panels.title: Tool call latency p95 by tool

panels.description: Model request rate by provider.
panels.title: Model request rate by provider

panels.description: Fraction of model requests returning result=error.
panels.title: Model error ratio

panels.description: p95 model request latency by provider.
panels.title: Model request latency p95 by provider

panels.description: Bytes elided per second by tool-output truncation. A sustained rate means tools are routinely exceeding the output cap; raise the cap or tighten the queries if context is being lost.
panels.title: Output truncation rate (bytes elided)

panels.description: Rate of alerts entering the coalescer, folded into existing batches, and suppressed by cooldown.
panels.title: Alert intake rate

panels.description: Distribution of incidents per flushed batch. A right-shifted distribution means the coalescer is folding many alerts together (good fan-in); a spike at 1 means little coalescing is happening.
panels.title: Coalesced batch size distribution

panels.description: Alerts that were still inside their debounce window when the process shut down. Alertmanager already got a 200, so it will not resend until its repeat_interval (often hours) — these alerts are simply never investigated. Expected to be rare, but it rises once per held alert on every restart or helm upgrade that lands mid-hold. Any sustained non-zero value is real alert loss: shorten triggers.incidents.debounce or set it to 0s.
panels.title: Alerts LOST on shutdown (should be zero)

panels.description: Where an `@runlore note:` landed. comment = added to the curated PR this thread came from, and is DISCARDED when that PR merges; open_pr = a standalone Concept entry PR; append = added to the entry file of the standalone PR an earlier note in this thread opened. open_pr + append are the notes that become durable catalog knowledge.
panels.title: Knowledge writes by route

panels.description: Note writes denied by the global per-hour forge-write window and told to retry. This is the feature's one global cap and nothing else reports it — sustained non-zero means humans are being turned away mid-incident.
panels.title: Thread writes throttled

panels.description: Model calls the chat layer made, against calls the per-hour budget refused. ceiling=tokens firing while call slots remain is the budget working as designed: the token ceiling is derived so a runaway of maximum-size calls is stopped by cost before it exhausts the call count.
panels.title: Chat calls vs denials

panels.description: Chat tokens are provider-reported where available, otherwise a conservative estimate. NOTHING converts them to currency — model.chat.pricing is read by nothing — so do that yourself at your provider's rate. mentions_dropped is note LOSS: the handler pool was saturated, the transport was already acked, and the human's note is gone.
panels.title: Chat tokens spent / mentions dropped

panels.description: Running image version (runlore_build_info). Deduplicated per distinct version, so a rollout shows old+new briefly, steady-state shows one.
panels.title: Agent version

panels.description: Elected leaders (healthy = 1). Bounded to a 1m window so a just-rolled replica's stale series doesn't linger; a transient 2 during a rollout is expected (yellow), 0 is a real problem (red).
panels.title: Active leaders

panels.description: Replicas that reported in the last minute (1m window excludes recently-terminated pods, so it doesn't over-count during rollouts).
panels.title: Replicas reporting
